title: Signature Beacon Tower Clock: The Harbour Light Movement
body:
Specifications. The Signature Beacon Tower Clock is an original Signature design for harbour and coastal towers, built as a flatbed movement 90 centimetres wide with a 1.5 metre pendulum and a 4 metre illuminated dial. Its going weight is 120 kilograms and its strike weight 100 kilograms, each hanging in a dedicated shaft. This is a Signature-original design, clearly labelled as such, and never presented as an authentic historic public record.

Mechanism. A double three-legged gravity escapement gives the pendulum a constant impulse regardless of wind load on the great dial, and a separate strike train sounds the hour on a single harbour bell. The dial is edge-lit at night so ships and harbour workers can read it from the water, and the hands are counterweighted in stainless steel to resist salt air.

Maintenance. Rinse salt deposits from the dial frame and hand fixings quarterly, oil the train annually, and inspect the weight lines for corrosion twice a year. The harbour environment is harder on a tower clock than an inland one, so the inspection interval is shorter by design.

Build and restoration guidance. Build the movement on a stainless bed frame, fit the dial glazing with marine seals, and prove the strike tone from the harbour entrance before commissioning. Keep a spare set of hand counterweights on site.

Tools. Marine sealant, stainless spanners, salt-rinse kit, oil cup.

Demonstration. This record's demo computes the Signature Beacon pendulum case in Python; its expected output was produced by running the program at build time, never hand-typed.

title: Signature Market Cross Clock: A Town-Square Turret Design
body:
Specifications. The Signature Market Cross Clock is an original Signature design for a town-square turret, with a compact flatbed movement 70 centimetres wide, a seconds pendulum, and two dials facing the square and the market hall. Its dials are 1.8 metres across with gilded Roman numerals, and its quarter chime sounds the Westminster sequence on four small bells. This is a Signature-original design, never an authentic historic record.

Mechanism. A deadbeat escapement keeps the compact movement accurate, and a chime barrel drives the four quarter bells in their programmed order. The two dials are driven from one motion work through bevel leading-off rods, so both faces always agree. The hour strike follows the quarters on a fifth, larger bell.

Maintenance. Oil the movement and chime train annually, check both dials for agreement monthly, and inspect the chime barrel pins at each quarterly visit. A market-square clock is heard all day, so a single wrong chime note is noticed at once.

Build and restoration guidance. Build the two dials from one full-size drawing so their numerals match exactly, balance all hands before fitting, and test the full hour of quarters and the hour strike from the square before handover.

Tools. Bevel gear gauge, gilding kit, chime chart, hand balancer.

Demonstration. This record's demo computes the Market Cross strike samples case in Python; its expected output was produced by running the program at build time, never hand-typed.

title: Signature Station Clock Tower: The Twin-Dial Terminus Design
body:
Specifications. The Signature Station Clock Tower is an original Signature design for railway termini, with a tall chamber carrying a flatbed movement and two 3 metre dials facing the concourse and the platforms. Its pendulum is 2 metres long for stability in a draughty station tower, and its drive is weight-driven with automatic electric rewinding so station staff never need to climb to wind it. This is a Signature-original design.

Mechanism. The long pendulum and gravity escapement resist the vibration and air currents of a busy station, and the auto-wind motor keeps the weights raised without a weekly winding visit. A slave output from the same movement drives platform repeater dials, so every dial in the station shows the same time.

Maintenance. Test the auto-wind cycle monthly, inspect the slave wiring at each visit, and check the long pendulum suspension for vibration wear. Log the rate daily for the first month, because station vibration settles the suspension in ways a quiet tower does not.

Build and restoration guidance. Mount the pendulum suspension on a vibration-isolated bracket, fit the auto-wind with a manual override, and prove all repeater dials agree before opening the station clock to the public.

Tools. Vibration meter, auto-wind tester, slave cable tester, rate log.

Demonstration. This record's demo computes the Station Tower pendulum case in Python; its expected output was produced by running the program at build time, never hand-typed.

title: Signature University Tower Clock: The College Bell Design
body:
Specifications. The Signature University Tower Clock is an original Signature design for a college tower, with a 1.2 metre pendulum, a 2.5 metre dial, and a chime that marks the academic hour rather than only the clock hour. Its strike train can be silenced during examination weeks by a simple lever in the chamber, and its dial is illuminated for evening lectures. This is a Signature-original design.

Mechanism. A deadbeat escapement and a compact going train keep the college clock accurate, and a silencing lever lifts the strike hammer clear of the bell without stopping the going train. The academic-hour chime is set by a separate cam that the college porter can adjust at the start of each term.

Maintenance. Oil annually, test the silencing lever before each examination period, and re-check the academic-hour cam at the start of every term. Keep the chamber log where the porter and the clock keeper can both write in it.

Build and restoration guidance. Fit the silencing lever where it can be reached without climbing, label it clearly, and prove that silencing never affects the going train or the dial hands.

Tools. Silencing-lever gauge, term cam chart, oil cup, chamber logbook.

Demonstration. This record's demo computes the University dial case in Python; its expected output was produced by running the program at build time, never hand-typed.

title: Signature Garden Folly Clock: A Small Ornamental Tower
body:
Specifications. The Signature Garden Folly Clock is an original Signature design for a small ornamental garden tower, with a movement only 45 centimetres wide, a 0.8 metre pendulum, and a single 1.2 metre dial. Its strike is a single soft bell, chosen so it carries across a garden without disturbing neighbours. This is a Signature-original design for a domestic-scale tower.

Mechanism. A compact deadbeat escapement and a short pendulum keep the folly clock accurate in a small chamber, and the single strike train sounds the hour only, with no quarters. The dial is hand-painted, and the hands are light aluminium so the small train is never overloaded.

Maintenance. Oil twice a year, because a small chamber heats and cools more than a great tower, and check the painted dial for weather damage each spring. Keep the chamber ventilated and the weight shaft screened against insects and nesting birds.

Build and restoration guidance. Build the chamber with a removable roof panel so the movement can be lifted out for service, and fit the dial glazing so it can be cleaned from inside without scaffolding.

Tools. Small-movement oilers, dial paint kit, insect mesh, roof-panel spanner.

Demonstration. This record's demo computes the Folly pendulum case in Python; its expected output was produced by running the program at build time, never hand-typed.

title: Signature Mill Tower Clock: The Factory Timekeeper Design
body:
Specifications. The Signature Mill Tower Clock is an original Signature design for a mill or factory tower, with a dust-resistant chamber, a 3 metre dial visible from the mill yard, and a loud hour bell that carries over machinery noise. Its movement is a robust flatbed 100 centimetres wide with a 1.5 metre pendulum, and its weight shaft is enclosed against dust. This is a Signature-original design.

Mechanism. A gravity escapement resists the vibration and dust load of a working mill, and the strike train drives a heavy hammer on a large bell. The dial is fitted with a washable glass cover, and the leading-off work is enclosed so dust cannot settle on the gearing.

Maintenance. Clean the chamber and dial cover monthly in a working mill, oil the train quarterly rather than annually, and inspect the enclosed shaft seals at each visit. Dust is the mill clock's main enemy, and the maintenance interval is set accordingly.

Build and restoration guidance. Fit dust seals to every chamber opening, enclose the leading-off work, and prove the bell tone from the far side of the mill yard before commissioning.

Tools. Dust seals, chamber brush, quarterly oil kit, tone logbook.

Demonstration. This record's demo computes the Mill great wheel stage case in Python; its expected output was produced by running the program at build time, never hand-typed.

title: Signature Lighthouse Tower Clock: The Coastal Signal Design
body:
Specifications. The Signature Lighthouse Tower Clock is an original Signature design that pairs a tower clock with a lighthouse station, using a 2 metre dial, a seconds pendulum, and a strike that sounds a fog-period pattern in poor visibility as well as the hour. Its chamber is built to lighthouse standards for salt, wind and vibration. This is a Signature-original design.

Mechanism. The gravity escapement and seconds pendulum keep time through gales, and a separate fog-pattern cam can sound the station's fog signal from the same bell train when visibility falls. The dial is backlit with a red-safe light that does not interfere with the lighthouse beam.

Maintenance. Inspect salt corrosion monthly, test the fog-pattern cam before the fog season, and keep the red-safe lighting separate from the main dial lighting circuit. Log every gale and its effect on the rate.

Build and restoration guidance. Build the chamber to lighthouse weather standards, fit the fog cam so it can be engaged without stopping the clock, and prove the dial lighting does not spill into the lightroom.

Tools. Salt-corrosion kit, fog-cam chart, red-safe lamp tester, gale log.

Demonstration. This record's demo computes the Lighthouse seconds pendulum beat case in Python; its expected output was produced by running the program at build time, never hand-typed.

title: Signature Church Tower Clock: The Parish Chime Design
body:
Specifications. The Signature Church Tower Clock is an original Signature design for a parish church tower, with a 2 metre dial, a 1.5 metre pendulum, and a full Westminster quarter chime on four bells plus an hour strike on the tenor. Its chamber is arranged so the clock keeper can wind and inspect it without entering the bell chamber. This is a Signature-original design.

Mechanism. A gravity escapement gives a steady rate despite the wind load on a church dial, and the chime barrel sounds the quarters in order. The hour strike is triggered from the same going train, and a silencing lever allows the chime to be stilled overnight by the parish's choice.

Maintenance. Oil annually, check the chime sequence at all four quarters quarterly, and inspect the bell frames with the bells' own maintenance cycle. Keep the winding route clear and lit, since a dark tower stair is a safety hazard.

Build and restoration guidance. Lay out the chamber so winding, oiling and chime inspection can all be done from one safe standing position, and fit the silencing lever at hand height with a clear label.

Tools. Chime chart, silencing-lever label kit, winding lamp, oil cup.

Demonstration. This record's demo computes the Parish chime samples case in Python; its expected output was produced by running the program at build time, never hand-typed.

title: Signature Observatory Tower Clock: The Meridian Dial Design
body:
Specifications. The Signature Observatory Tower Clock is an original Signature design for an observatory tower, with a precision deadbeat escapement, a 2 metre compensated pendulum, and a dial that shows mean time alongside a sidereal indication for telescope work. Its chamber is temperature-controlled to protect the rate. This is a Signature-original design.

Mechanism. The compensated pendulum resists temperature change, and the deadbeat escapement gives the steady beat an observatory needs. Extra gearing drives a sidereal pointer that gains about four minutes per day against mean time, matching the stars' apparent motion, and the two indications are read together for observing sessions.

Maintenance. Log the chamber temperature with the rate, oil sparingly to avoid temperature-sensitive drag, and check the sidereal indication against a star almanac monthly. Keep the chamber door closed during observations to hold the temperature steady.

Build and restoration guidance. Build the temperature control before the movement arrives, fit the compensated pendulum to the maker's specification, and prove the sidereal gearing over a full month against almanac data.

Tools. Temperature logger, almanac, compensated-pendulum gauge, fine oilers.

Demonstration. This record's demo computes the sidereal ratio stage case in Python; its expected output was produced by running the program at build time, never hand-typed.

title: Signature Castle Tower Clock: The Fortress Dial Design
body:
Specifications. The Signature Castle Tower Clock is an original Signature design for a castle tower, with a stone dial 3.5 metres across, iron hands, a 2 metre pendulum, and a strike bell loud enough to be heard across the castle grounds. Its movement is housed in a vaulted chamber with a guarded winding stair. This is a Signature-original design.

Mechanism. A gravity escapement and heavy flatbed frame suit the draughts and temperature swings of a stone castle tower, and the iron hands are counterweighted to resist gales across the battlements. The strike train sounds the hour on a single great bell hung in the tower above the chamber.

Maintenance. Inspect the stone dial fixings annually, oil the train before winter, and check the winding stair guard at each visit. Castle towers are cold and damp, so the chamber needs ventilation without draughts across the pendulum.

Build and restoration guidance. Fix the dial into the stonework with stainless anchors, balance the iron hands on a knife edge before fitting, and prove the strike tone from the castle courtyard.

Tools. Stone anchors, iron-hand balancer, winter oil kit, stair guard gauge.

title: Signature Village Green Clock: The Community Tower Design
body:
Specifications. The Signature Village Green Clock is an original Signature design for a freestanding village clock tower, with a single 2 metre dial, a seconds pendulum, and an hour strike on a modest bell. Its chamber is at ground level behind a locked door, so the village clock keeper can wind it without climbing a tower. This is a Signature-original design.

Mechanism. A deadbeat escapement and seconds pendulum keep the village clock accurate, and a long leading-off rod carries the motion work up the tower to the dial. The ground-level chamber makes weekly winding a simple task, which is why the design suits a community keeper rather than a specialist.

Maintenance. Wind weekly, oil annually, and check the leading-off rod alignment each spring, since ground movement can shift a freestanding tower. Keep the chamber door lock working and the key with a named keeper.

Build and restoration guidance. Build the tower foundation deep enough to resist frost heave, fit the leading-off rod in sections for servicing, and prove the dial reads clearly from every side of the green.

Tools. Foundation gauge, leading-off rod spanners, keeper's key log, oil cup.

Demonstration. This record's demo computes the Village Green dial case in Python; its expected output was produced by running the program at build time, never hand-typed.

title: Signature Hospital Tower Clock: The Quiet-Hours Design
body:
Specifications. The Signature Hospital Tower Clock is an original Signature design for a hospital tower, with a 3 metre illuminated dial, a 1.5 metre pendulum, and a strike that is automatically silenced at night and softened during the day. Its movement is weight-driven with auto-wind, so hospital staff never need to wind it. This is a Signature-original design.

Mechanism. A gravity escapement keeps the rate steady, and a time-controlled silencing cam lifts the strike hammer clear during quiet hours and returns it for daytime hours. The dial lighting is dimmed at night to avoid light spill into wards, while remaining readable from the hospital grounds.

Maintenance. Test the quiet-hours cam weekly, inspect the auto-wind monthly, and check dial dimming at night from the wards. Log any night strike immediately, since a night strike in a hospital is a fault to fix, not a curiosity.

Build and restoration guidance. Fit the quiet-hours cam with a manual override for emergencies, label the override clearly, and prove the night silence over a full week before handover.

Tools. Quiet-hours cam chart, auto-wind tester, night-dimming meter, fault log.

Demonstration. This record's demo computes the monthly auto-wind check case in Python; its expected output was produced by running the program at build time, never hand-typed.

title: Signature Museum Tower Clock: The Working Exhibit Design
body:
Specifications. The Signature Museum Tower Clock is an original Signature design for a museum tower, with a glass-fronted chamber so visitors can watch the flatbed movement, a 1.5 metre pendulum, and a 2 metre dial. Its strike is demonstrated on the hour during opening hours and silenced when the museum is closed. This is a Signature-original design.

Mechanism. A deadbeat escapement and a well-lit movement make the working mechanism the exhibit, and the glass front is fitted so visitors can see the train, escapement and pendulum without touching them. A demonstration lever lets a guide trigger a single strike for a tour group without waiting for the hour.

Maintenance. Clean the glass weekly, oil the movement on a museum schedule that avoids open hours, and test the demonstration lever before each tour day. Keep the chamber lighting cool, so heat does not affect the pendulum rate during the day.

Build and restoration guidance. Build the glass front with a locked service panel, fit cool lighting, and prove the demonstration strike cannot double-strike or jam the hour strike.

Tools. Glass cleaner, cool-light meter, demonstration-lever gauge, tour log.

Demonstration. This record's demo computes the Museum seconds pendulum beat case in Python; its expected output was produced by running the program at build time, never hand-typed.

title: Signature Winter Tower Clock: The Cold-Climate Design
body:
Specifications. The Signature Winter Tower Clock is an original Signature design for cold climates, with an insulated chamber, a temperature-compensated 2 metre pendulum, a heated dial glazing system, and a gravity escapement chosen for steady running through freeze and thaw. Its dial is 3 metres across and its hands are fitted with ice-shedding profiles. This is a Signature-original design.

Mechanism. The compensated pendulum resists the large temperature swings of a cold-climate tower, and the heated glazing keeps the dial readable through frost and rime. The gravity escapement tolerates the extra load when ice forms on the hands, and the chamber insulation keeps the movement itself near a stable temperature.

Maintenance. Check the glazing heater before the first frost, inspect hand profiles for ice damage after storms, and log the rate against temperature through the winter. Oil with a cold-rated clock oil, since ordinary oil thickens in a cold chamber.

Build and restoration guidance. Fit the insulation and heater before the movement arrives, prove the dial stays clear through a frost test, and set the compensated pendulum to the maker's cold-climate specification.

Tools. Cold-rated oil, glazing heater tester, ice-profile gauge, temperature log.

Demonstration. This record's demo computes the Winter pendulum, cold chamber case in Python; its expected output was produced by running the program at build time, never hand-typed.

title: Signature Solar Tower Clock: The Sun-Powered Dial Design
body:
Specifications. The Signature Solar Tower Clock is an original Signature design for a sunny site, with solar panels on the tower roof charging a battery that powers the dial drive and LED illumination. Its dial is 2.5 metres across, its pendulum is a 1.2 metre compensated pendulum, and its drive is a stepping motor under radio correction. This is a Signature-original design.

Mechanism. Solar power charges the battery by day, and the battery drives the stepping motor and the LED dial lighting at night. The radio correction keeps the dial exact, and the compensated pendulum is retained as a visible working regulator in the chamber, even though the dial drive is electric, so visitors can see a real pendulum at work.

Maintenance. Clean the solar panels quarterly, test the battery capacity annually, and check the radio correction log monthly. Keep the pendulum oiled and beating, since it is the visible heart of the exhibit even when the dial drive is electric.

Build and restoration guidance. Size the battery for at least five sunless days, fit the panels where they can be cleaned safely, and prove the system through a simulated power cut before commissioning.

Tools. Solar panel brush, battery capacity tester, radio log, pendulum oil kit.

Demonstration. This record's demo computes the Solar dial case in Python; its expected output was produced by running the program at build time, never hand-typed.

title: Signature Grand Terminus Tower Clock: The Four-Face Master Design
body:
Specifications. The Signature Grand Terminus Tower Clock is an original Signature design for a great station or civic tower, with four 4 metre dials, one on each face, a 2 metre pendulum, a gravity escapement, and a full Westminster chime on five bells. Its movement is a large flatbed 120 centimetres wide, and its weight shafts run the full height of the tower. This is a Signature-original design, the most complex in this Signature set.

Mechanism. One going train drives all four dials through bevel leading-off work, so the four faces can never disagree. The chime barrel sounds the quarters on four bells, the hour strike follows on the great bell, and an auto-wind system keeps the great weights raised. The gravity escapement isolates the pendulum from the wind load of four great dials, which is the central engineering problem of a four-face tower.

Maintenance. Inspect all four dials and their leading-off work quarterly, oil the great movement annually, test the auto-wind monthly, and listen to the full chime and strike sequence from all four sides of the tower at least once a year.

Build and restoration guidance. Build the four dials from one drawing, balance all eight hands before fitting, align the bevel work face by face, and prove four-face agreement and the full chime sequence from the ground on all sides before handover.

Tools. Four-face alignment gauge, bevel spanners, chime chart, auto-wind tester.

Demonstration. This record's demo computes the Grand Terminus motion-work stage case in Python; its expected output was produced by running the program at build time, never hand-typed.
